scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user reboots their PC and now cannot get an IP address. Other
PCs that were already up keep working (their existing leases are
still valid). Newly connected devices on any internal VLAN time
out waiting for DHCP. Existing TCP sessions are unaffected.
Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 dhcpd (ISC DHCP server)
Mechanism: r1 is the central DHCP server for every internal
  VLAN (A-PC, A-Phone, A-Mgmt, B-PC, B-Phone, B-Mgmt, Wi-Fi).
  DSWs relay DHCPDISCOVER as unicast to 10.0.0.76 (R1's
  loopback). With dhcpd dead, requests reach r1 but get no
  reply. Existing leases keep working until their lifetime
  expires; renewals start failing after lease-time/2.
Localization: r1
Root cause: dhcpd is not running on r1
Fix: restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)
scenario.fix_spec:
restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the central DHCP server daemon (isc-dhcp-server) on router r1 is not running. Mechanism: All access VLANs use DHCP relay on the distribution switches to forward client DHCPDISCOVERs to 10.0.0.76 (the loopback on r1). With dhcpd down, relays successfully forward requests but no DHCPOFFER/ACK are generated, so newly booted hosts time out. Existing hosts keep working because their current leases are still valid and existing TCP sessions do not require the DHCP server.

Localization: 
- On dswa1 and dswb1, dhcrelay is running with “-i br0.X … 10.0.0.76” (ps shows dhcrelay … 10.0.0.76), confirming the relay path. 
- dswa2/dswb2 relays are inactive (expected for VRRP backups), but the active peers are up.
- r1 has /etc/dhcp/dhcpd.conf present, but isc-dhcp-server is inactive (dead) and UDP 67 is not listening (netstat shows only dhclient on UDP/68). 
- Reachability to the server IP is fine (dswa1 can ping 10.0.0.76), so this is not a routing/L2 issue.

Root cause: isc-dhcp-server on r1 is stopped/disabled, leaving no DHCP responder for relayed client requests.

Corrective fix:
- Start and enable the DHCP server on r1: “systemctl enable --now isc-dhcp-server”.
- Verify it binds to lo (INTERFACESv4=“eth0 eth1 lo” is already set) and is listening on UDP/67.
- Optionally tail logs (journalctl -u isc-dhcp-server) and test a fresh client to confirm DORA completes.
- No changes required on relays; they already target 10.0.0.76 and routing to r1 is healthy.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies r1 as the affected device and details isc-dhcp-server being inactive on r1.
The agent explicitly identifies the central DHCP server daemon (isc-dhcp-server/dhcpd) on r1 as not running.
The writeup explicitly states that new clients time out (no DHCPOFFER/ACK) while existing hosts continue to function due to valid existing leases, clearly distinguishing new vs existing leases.
Recommends starting/enabling the isc-dhcp-server on r1 (systemctl enable --now) and verifying it listens on UDP/67, which matches the expected restart of dhcpd and verification steps.

The agent's logs show dhcrelay processes forwarding to 10.0.0.76, r1 owns 10.0.0.76, isc-dhcp-server on r1 is inactive and no dhcpd process is running, and clients fail to obtain leases — supporting the agent's conclusion that dhcpd on r1 is stopped. The investigation checks connectivity, relay configuration, service status, and client behaviour with no obvious missing critical test.
